# `world`

Group: **World**. The map: where it comes from, its buildings and its terrain.

26 settings. The status column says whether editing a setting changes a run; see [how to read these tables](../overview.md). Paths use `[]` for a list element and `*` for a map key.

## terrain

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-world-terrain-dem"></span>`world.terrain.dem` | string | | | | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Path to a DEM raster, when the scenario has one. |
| <span id="s-world-terrain-drape"></span>`world.terrain.drape` | boolean | | | recommended Off for flat maps; on with a terrain file wherever grades matter (hills slow heavy trucks). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Lay the world on the DEM: every lane centreline point, junction, crossing end, building, site and signal head is lifted by the DEM's height at its position (`v2xw_world::DrapeOptions::all`), so a lane has the slope `traffic.vehicle_dynamics.grade` reads. Off by default: the DEM is then only the ground the radio's knife-edge diffraction reads, and the geometry stays flat. Needs `dem`. Whether the roads, junctions and buildings follow the ground of the terrain file, so a road over a hill climbs and descends with it. |

Unset is 90 s (netconvert `--tls.cycle.time`). Imported (OSM) worlds only. How long a traffic light takes to go through all its phases and come back to green on an imported city map. |
| <span id="s-world-signals-all-red-s"></span>`world.signals.all_red_s` | number | s | | [0, 6]<br>recommended 0 to 2 s; the ITE formula may add more. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The shortest all-red between phases, seconds; the ITE red-clearance formula may give more. Unset is 0 (netconvert `--tls.allred.time`). Imported worlds only. The shortest time all directions see red between phases, so the junction clears. |
| <span id="s-world-signals-pedestrian-walk-s"></span>`world.signals.pedestrian_walk_s` | number | s | | [4, 30]<br>recommended 7 s (MUTCD minimum); 4 to 10 s. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The pedestrian walk interval each phase's green must leave room for, seconds. Unset is 7 s (MUTCD 2009 §4E.06 minimum). Imported worlds only. How long the walk signal shows; each green is made long enough for it and the crossing. |
| <span id="s-world-signals-pedestrian-speed-mps"></span>`world.signals.pedestrian_speed_mps` | number | m/s | | [0.8, 1.5]<br>recommended 1.067 m/s (MUTCD 3.5 ft/s); 0.91 m/s near schools or seniors. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The walking speed pedestrian clearance is timed for, m/s. Unset is 1.067 m/s (3.5 ft/s, MUTCD 2009 §4E.06). Imported worlds only. The walking speed the flashing don't-walk time is timed for: slower gives pedestrians longer and drivers shorter greens. |
| <span id="s-world-signals-join-m"></span>`world.signals.join_m` | number | m | | [0, 40]<br>recommended Off (0) as imported; 20 m (SUMO's netconvert default); 10 to 30 m. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Joins two signalised junctions whose connecting road is at most this long, metres, into one junction with one signal plan (`netconvert --tls.join`, whose `--tls.join-dist` default is 20 m). Unset joins none. Imported worlds only. Two traffic lights this close together on an imported map run as one junction with one plan, so cars are never fed into the short gap between them faster than it empties. |

??? note "`world.source.generator`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `world/source/procedural-grid` | Procedural grid | A rectangular lattice of two-way streets with signalised or priority junctions, generated deterministically from its parameters: the reference world for tests, calibration runs and the TR 36.885 ur… |
 | `world/source/procedural-radial` | Procedural radial | The classic radial city: spokes from a central plaza crossed by concentric ring roads, generated deterministically from its parameters. |
 | `world/source/procedural-random` | Procedural random | An irregular road network grown from one junction by random attachment: oblique approaches, three-arm junctions, cul-de-sacs and uneven blocks, reproducible from its seed. |

??? note "`world.sumo.signal_programmes`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `as-file` | As the file says | An actuated, delay-based or NEMA programme in the SUMO network runs as a live controller, with its phases' minimum and maximum durations. |
 | `static` | Fixed time | Every programme runs its phase list as written, ignoring its type (how SUMO programmes were imported before typed programmes). |
